passages.title: The Monday Notice
passages.direction: Read evenly and clearly at a moderate pace, with no performance. This is your baseline voice — every other passage is measured against it.

cards.text: It is seven in the morning on Monday, the twelfth of April, and the workshop opened on time.
Quang checked forty-eight crates, wrote the figures into the log book, and signed his name.
The old machine runs far more quietly since we replaced the belt and oiled the main shaft.
Please keep your distance from the press, wear a mask, and switch the lights off on your way out.
Order number three seven two one covers ninety-five metres of fabric, delivered before three in the afternoon.
Today it is twenty-nine degrees, humidity seventy percent, with a light breeze from the south-east.
I T will update the E R P software tonight, so log out before the system restarts.
The new shop on the south side opens at the end of the month, and we expect roughly three hundred visitors.
Send your report before Friday, either by email or straight to the desk at reception.
If anything is unclear, call zero nine one, two three four, five six seven eight.
The cold store holds minus eighteen degrees and is checked twice every day.
Thank you for reading to the end of the notice, and have a smooth day at work.

passages.title: Articulation Drill
passages.direction: Slow and separated. Do not run words together. Clarity matters, speed does not. Leave half a second between groups.

cards.text: Thin, then, thing, think, this, those. Six words, each one fully finished.
The sixth sick sheikh's sixth sheep is sleeping in the shed.
Red leather, yellow leather, red lorry, yellow lorry, said slowly and clearly.
Strengths, twelfths, sixths, glimpsed. Four clusters that most people rush.
Bought, boat, bout, bot, but, boot. Six vowels, one consonant frame.
Particularly, February, library, February again, and then rural juror.
A proper copper coffee pot, poured properly, twice over.
Measure, pleasure, treasure, closure. Keep the ending soft, never sharp.
Whether the weather is warm, whether the weather is cold, we will go.
Eleven benevolent elephants walked evenly along the eastern edge.

passages.title: Walking Through The Steps
passages.direction: Explaining to a colleague. Level, unhurried, one short beat between steps.

cards.text: There are four steps, and we will go through them one at a time.
Step one, check the power supply and make sure the indicator light is green.
Step two, open the rear panel, lift the tray out, and set it on a dry surface.
Step three, wipe the dust away with a soft cloth. No water, and no alcohol.
Step four, put everything back in the order you removed it, finger tight, never forced.
If the indicator turns amber, stop there and call the technical team.
The whole routine takes about fifteen minutes once your hands know it.
Write the date in the log afterwards, so next time you know where you stand.
On any machine older than three years, do this every two months.
If something is unclear, ask. Do not guess and carry on.

passages.title: It Is Actually Happening
passages.direction: High energy, quick pace, pitch a little above your normal register. Do not shout — push from the belly, keep the volume moderate and let the rhythm carry it.

cards.text: That is it, the tickets are booked! Three in the morning and we are on the road!
You will not believe it. The place we have talked about for two years, and we are finally going!
I just opened the map, and there is a whole stretch of that road running along the coast!
Camera charged, two spare batteries, and sixty-four gigabytes still free on the card!
If we get up early enough we will catch the sunrise right at the top of the pass. Picture that!
They say the little place up there opens at five, so we will be the first ones through the door!
Everyone said yes. Nobody is busy, nobody is stuck at work. What are the odds!
I printed the plan and stuck it on the fridge so I can look at it once a day and calm down!
Ten hours to go! I am going to pack, because I cannot sit still any longer!
And if the weather holds, honestly, it does not get better than this!

passages.title: My Disciplined Morning
passages.direction: Deadpan. Leave half a beat before the last line of each card. If a laugh or a breath escapes, keep it — that is exactly what we want on tape.

cards.text: This morning I got up a full thirty minutes early, determined to be a disciplined person for once.
I made coffee, opened the laptop, and sat up straight like the people in productivity videos.
Four minutes in, the cat walked across the keyboard and produced a longer document than mine.
The troubling part is that hers made more sense than what I wrote last night.
I moved her off the desk, and she looked at me like someone who had just been robbed.
At eight o'clock I remembered that it was Sunday.
So all that discipline, spent entirely on the one day that did not need any.
I closed the laptop and went down to the kitchen, and the cat went straight back to the desk.
She is sitting in my chair now. Back straight. Very serious face.
At least somebody in this house is disciplined.

passages.title: Saying It Out Loud
passages.direction: Warm, unhurried, open throat, sentences settling downward at the end. Speak as if sitting beside one friend, not addressing a room.

cards.text: Thank you for staying until the end today. I know that was not easy.
What you did last week genuinely helped. I am not saying that to be nice.
Everyone on the team noticed. Most of them just never say it out loud.
I like how steady you stay when everything is coming apart. Not many people can do that.
You may not see the result yet, but the foundation you are laying is solid.
Keep the same pace. There is no rush, and nothing to prove to anybody.
If you want someone to listen, I am here. I am really not that busy.
We still have a long way to go, but it is lighter when we walk it together.
I am honestly glad to see you sounding like yourself again.
Go and rest. We will start again tomorrow, slowly.

passages.title: End Of A Long Day
passages.direction: Low pitch, short breath, slow, sentences falling away at the end. Let yourself breathe mid-sentence and let a line run out of air — that is the signal we are capturing.

cards.text: That was a long day. I did not think it would be that long.
I am going to sit here for a minute. Just a minute, then I will get up.
I have had the coffee. Three cups of it. My eyes are still closing.
Whatever is left, it can wait until tomorrow. I will start early.
I am not ill tired. I am just out of battery.
Talking feels heavy. Thinking feels heavy. Everything is running slower than usual.
That list has been open since this morning and I have not crossed off a single line.
All right. I am shutting the machine down. Tomorrow.
It will probably be better tomorrow. It usually is.
I am going to bed. Good night, everyone.

passages.title: The Room Has Not Changed
passages.direction: Slow, quiet, plenty of silence, low and fairly level pitch. Sad, not sobbing — if the voice breaks, that belongs to the Tearful passage instead.

cards.text: The room has not changed at all. There is just nobody in the chair by the window.
I still make two cups of tea, and only remember afterwards that one is enough.
Some afternoons I stand in the hallway for a very long time, doing nothing.
People say you get used to it. I have not got used to any of it.
The coat is still hanging there. I have not been brave enough to put it away.
I miss the voice, the footsteps, even the way the door was knocked three times.
Everything keeps running. The city is still loud. Only the house is quiet.
I am not angry with anyone. I am only sorry.
If I had stayed ten minutes longer that day.
It is late. I am going to turn the light off.

passages.title: The Sentence I Never Said
passages.direction: Broken voice, unsteady breath, catching air mid-sentence, sometimes barely audible. You do not have to actually cry — keep the breath broken and the throat tight. Skip this passage if it is too much; it is optional.

cards.text: I am sorry. I cannot get a single sentence out properly.
I practised this the whole way here, and now I am standing here I have forgotten all of it.
I remember you walking me over that bridge when I was small. Every morning.
I really thought there was so much more time.
I did not get back in time. I am sorry that I did not get back in time.
There was so much I meant to tell you and I never told you any of it.
I love you. I never once managed to say that properly.
I promise I will live well. Please stop worrying about me.
All right. I am going now. I will come back again.
Sleep well. I will come and sit with you again.

passages.title: The Third Time
passages.direction: Start clamped down, each word squeezed, then build. Do not shout — support from the belly, moderate volume, high pressure. Shouting clips the take and wastes the card.

cards.text: Listen to me. I have raised this three times now. Three.
I do not need another explanation from you.
Every time this happens, the whole team starts again from nothing.
Do you have any idea what time people were still here last night?
No, you do not, because you shut your machine and went home.
I can live with mistakes. Everybody makes them. I cannot live with being ignored.
That is enough. From now on, whatever you take on, you finish.
Stop handing it to somebody else. I mean it.
I do not want to have this conversation one more time.
Go on, step outside. I need a minute.

passages.title: Notes On The Proposal
passages.direction: Calm, sharp, final. Not loud, but cold. Land hard on the opening consonants, break the clauses clearly, and never let a line rise at the end.

cards.text: I have read the whole proposal, and I will say plainly that it is not good enough.
The figures on page three contradict the conclusion on page seven.
Anyone reading carefully will see it, so do not assume the client will not.
The presentation is handsome. Handsome does not replace substance.
Three of the four assumptions here carry no source at all.
As a draft, this is fine. As something we put in front of a client, it is not.
I am not judging the person. I am judging this document.
And this document reads like it was done in a hurry.
Rebuild section two, verify every figure, and send it to me on Thursday morning.
I will read it again. As closely as I read this one.
